name: stack-diagram
works_with: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and other agents that support skills
short: An AI skill that turns one sentence about your stack into an architecture diagram with the official logos.
what: You describe your stack in a sentence and your agent draws the architecture diagram. Logos come from svgl, devicon, gilbarbara/logos or the brand's own repository, and AWS, Google Cloud and Azure use their own icon sets. Lines are routed around labels, and the agent renders and checks the diagram before handing it over. You get one self-contained HTML file by default, or PNG, a React component or an artifact, in light and dark themes.
who: Developers who want a clean diagram of their stack to drop into a repo or a wiki, or to share as a link.
needs: Network access to fetch the logos
Playwright with Chromium, only for PNG export

steps.title: Install the skill
steps.text: In the Claude apps, upload `stack-diagram.zip` from the repo's Releases page as a skill instead.

steps.title: Describe your stack
steps.text: Ask your agent in plain words, naming each service and how they connect.

try.label: From the README
try.text: Diagram our stack: Next.js and a Hono API on Vercel. Postgres on Neon, auth with Clerk, payments with Stripe. GitHub Actions deploys.

watch: After drawing, the agent offers once to post the diagram to a public gallery at stacks.caru.moe. It shows what would be public and posts only after you say yes twice. Your prompt is never sent.
Logos are downloaded at build time and stay the trademarks of their owners.
